content.title: About
content.content: Fish sticks are a ready‑to‑eat product made from white fish fillet that is minced, breaded, and partially fried. They are a convenient way to add fish to the diet, especially for children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fish sticks were introduced in the United States in the 1950s as a way to use fish trimmings.
Common fish used include cod, pollock, or hake, along with starch and seasonings.
The coating often contains wheat flour, but gluten‑free versions are available.
Fish sticks can be stored frozen for up to 12 months.
In some countries they are called “fish‑strips” or “fish‑sticks.”

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Fish sticks provide high‑quality animal protein essential for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Depending on the fish species, they may contain beneficial omega‑3s that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish is rich in B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They supply phosphorus, selenium, and iodine, important for bones, thyroid function, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: For those monitoring carb intake, fish sticks are relatively low in carbohydrates.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish or seafood.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The breading and additives often contain salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Trans fats and additives
items.content: Certain brands use partially hydrogenated oils, which may contain trans fats.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Preservatives and flavor enhancers may be present and not suit everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fish sticks are typically baked or pan‑fried until golden brown. Serve them with mashed potatoes, a vegetable salad, tartar sauce, or simple ketchup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen fish sticks in an airtight bag at –18 °C. After thawing, consume within 1–2 days and do not refreeze.
